claims.text: ARP: to send to an IP address on its own network, a machine asks every machine on that network who has the address; the holder replies with its hardware (MAC) address, and the asker keeps the answer in an ARP table and sends packets there.
claims.source_hint: metallb.io Configuration > Layer 2 ('responding to ARP requests ... to give the machine's MAC address to clients'); RFC 826 (broadcast request); capture metallb-l2.txt

claims.text: In layer 2 mode, which an L2Advertisement asks for, MetalLB's speakers choose one node per Service address, and only that node's speaker answers ARP requests for it.
claims.source_hint: metallb.io: Concepts > MetalLB in layer 2 mode ('one machine in the cluster takes ownership of the service'); Configuration > Layer 2

claims.text: In layer 2 mode the Service address is not configured on any network card of the announcing node; the speaker only answers ARP for it.
claims.source_hint: metallb.io Configuration > Layer 2 (addresses need not be bound to node interfaces); Concepts > Layer 2; a capture of `ip -4 addr` on the node would settle it (repo_changes_needed)

claims.text: kube-proxy on a node has rules for a LoadBalancer Service's outside address (status.loadBalancer.ingress), as for its cluster IP, and forwards each connection to a ready Pod on that node or another (externalTrafficPolicy Cluster, the default).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Virtual IPs and Service Proxies (iptables mode, load balancer IPs); Services > type: LoadBalancer; metallb.io Concepts > Layer 2 ('kube-proxy spreads traffic')

claims.text: In layer 2 mode all traffic for one Service address enters through the single announcing node, so its incoming traffic is limited to that node's link; other nodes receive only connections it forwards to their Pods. The speakers may pick different nodes for different addresses.
claims.source_hint: metallb.io: Concepts > Layer 2 > Limitations ('Single-node bottlenecking'); Load-balancing behavior

claims.text: When the announcing node fails, the other speakers detect it and another node takes over announcing the address automatically.
claims.source_hint: metallb.io: Concepts > Layer 2 ('If the leader node fails ... failover is automatic')

claims.text: On failover, the new announcing node sends unsolicited (gratuitous) ARP messages so clients learn the address's new hardware address; until a client does, its packets still go to the old node and calls fail.
claims.source_hint: metallb.io: Concepts > Layer 2 > Limitations ('Potentially slow failover', gratuitous layer 2 packets)

claims.text: Layer 2 mode does not implement load balancing across nodes; it implements a failover mechanism so another node can take over the address.
claims.source_hint: metallb.io: Concepts > Layer 2 ('layer 2 does not implement a load balancer. Rather, it implements a failover mechanism')
